R1.outcome: Pre-land drift and inner-push non_fast_forward now resetGroup (re-queue) instead of rejectGroup, matching what the single-repo lane has always done. A race's attempt is cancelled, not failed. auth/network/other still reject. Bounded at 4 integration attempts DERIVED from attempt rows (no migration); past it the reject names lane contention, not the change. An unreadable count re-queues anyway.
R1.expected_impact: The fix for the reported 'main moved and it got rejected' pain.

R2.why: Premise verified false. worktree.resetForAttempt() fetches + hard-resets to origin/main before EVERY attempt, so an assembly rebase never runs against a stale base and a retry would hit the identical conflict. The real staleness window (main moving during a long verify) is covered by R1's re-queue.

R3.outcome: notify_author_on_reject (default false): a reject raises an escalation addressed to the submitting worker so the existing wake daemon delivers it into their session.
R3.trap_pinned: The escalation must belong to the WORKER with the notice authored by the TRAIN — the daemon delivers 'messages not authored by the origin author', so the natural implementation would wake nobody, silently.

R4.outcome: inner_conflict on a cross-repo group is now actually resolved: a second resolver pool cloned from the INNER repo (own slots, non-fatal if unbuildable), replay inputs (base/ref/files) carried on AssembledGroupErr before release(), and a group resubmit as an inner-only group (synthesizeOuter) so the resolved inner cannot land without its outer bump.
R4.scope_note: Only inner_conflict is EXECUTED. gitlink_diverged stays eligible-but-unexecuted: hasRemainingMarkers() is a marker-reconciliation criterion and would declare a bump rebase done while nothing was fixed.

R5.outcome: rejectGroupLegibly → maybeOpenResolution, gated on eligibility (judgement) AND the replay payload (capability) as two separate conditions. No-recursion guard moved upstream to the origin, because the group resubmit takes member specs with no resolvedFrom to carry. Guide §14.18/§14.19/§14.20 + CLAUDE.md capability index.

verification.integrator: 42 test files green (group-integration 20/20 incl. 3 new R5 hook tests; group-land 9/9 incl. 3 new R1 tests)
verification.gates: typecheck + lint + format:check + build all pass
verification.e2e: 38/39. The single failure is 07-claims-surface stale-lease timing — a known pre-existing flake unrelated to the merge train (it also flaked during the 2026-08-14 campaign); passes 8/8 in isolation, verified twice.

deployment.pm_server: redeploy picks up notify_author_on_reject and the reject notification
deployment.daemon: rebundle + restart required for R1 (re-queue), R4 (inner resolver pool) and R5 (the hook)
deployment.opt_in: notify_author_on_reject must be turned ON per project. The inner resolver pool only builds when resolver.enabled is true AND linked_repos declares an inner repo.

follow_ups: gitlink_diverged needs its own completion criterion before it can be executed (it is eligible today but not runnable).

outer_conflict is eligible and has replay inputs in principle, but no outer resolver pool is built — only inner. Add one if outer conflicts turn out to be common after the stale-bump class is eliminated by synthesize_outer.
R3 delivers only on REJECT. A group that exhausts R1's re-queue bound rejects, so it is covered; a request abandoned by a human is not.
